# Traefik — root-context

App at /, proxy at /. Baseline Traefik scenario: one router, one service, and no WebSocket configuration at all, because Traefik upgrades on every route when the client asks.

Proxy URL on `http://localhost:9090`: `/`

## Configuration

See [docker-compose.yml](./docker-compose.yml) for service definitions.

Traefik dynamic config (`vaadin.yml`), mounted into
`/etc/traefik/dynamic`:

```yaml
# Baseline: app at /, proxy at /. One router, one service, nothing else.
#
# There is no WebSocket configuration because Traefik has none to give: every
# router upgrades when the client asks. Compare apache-httpd's
# `upgrade=websocket` and NGINX's `map $http_upgrade` + Upgrade/Connection
# headers, both of which this file does without.
http:
  routers:
    vaadin:
      rule: PathPrefix(`/`)
      entryPoints:
        - web
      middlewares:
        - compress
      service: vaadin

  services:
    vaadin:
      loadBalancer:
        servers:
          - url: http://vaadin:8080

  middlewares:
    # Compression on, the way a real deployment has it — but never over a
    # streamed response. Where NGINX has an allowlist (gzip_types) this is a
    # denylist, so the streamed types must be named: Traefik's compress
    # middleware does not skip text/event-stream on its own, and its
    # minResponseBodyBytes default of 1024 means an un-excluded stream is held
    # until a kilobyte accumulates. text/event-stream is SSE push; text/plain
    # is streaming and long polling (PushHandler sets that content type).
    compress:
      compress:
        excludedContentTypes:
          - text/event-stream
          - text/plain
```

The entryPoints and the file provider come from the shared
[traefik.yml](../../traefik.yml), mounted read-only.
